svg.text: A heterogeneous fleet, honestly modelled
mac does not pretend every machine is the same server class. Node classes differ by supervisor, isolation model and hardware, and the ADRs say which is which.
hub
ledger · capability registry · capacity · dispatch
macOS node
ADR 0015 · Accepted
Host install under launchd. Not a container.
The earlier attempt ran the Linux-ELF OpenShell
gateway inside a Linux container on Docker; that
amendment was superseded.
Native toolchains, Apple silicon, and Xcode-bound
work are reachable because the agent is a host
process rather than a guest.
Linux node
Native steward under systemd, with task
execution in containers. The containerized half of
ADR 0012 now applies to Linux only.
OpenShell owns isolation — process trees,
filesystem and network policy, sandbox lifecycle,
and normalized action events.
Docker Engine / Moby is the only container runtime.
Kubernetes / HGX
elastic capacity
Pods under supervisord. The runner carries
independent build and review paths, wrapped by
mac-owned test, evidence and publication gates.
HGX capacity is elastic: the fleet asks for more
workers when saturated rather than queueing behind
a fixed pool.
GPU facts are part of the capability registry.
What actually runs the work
Five coding-agent routes, each with its own identity, discovered where it is
installed. The sandbox derives its available agents from the router rather than
hardcoding a list, so adding a route does not fork the image definition.
claude
codex
cursor
opencode
pi
A preflight sentinel proves the sandbox can actually launch the chosen agent before work is dispatched into it, and the
MCP config the sandbox writes is asserted by test to launch mac's own ledger server — so the socket is never wired to nothing.
Sandbox policy changes are announced on the bus and acted on between tasks, not mid-flight.
Images and rollout
Runtime manifests are reproducible, with stable
digests and secret-value checks.
Images are qualified before use and carry a
tested-<inputs-sha> tag, so "which image was this
proven against" is answerable from the tag alone.
A synchronized cutover protocol moves the fleet
between qualified versions as a transaction.
A rollout can require a passing eval_run before promote.
Identity, secrets and blast radius
Secrets are handles, not values. Tenant-scoped secret handles carry audit records, and API and CLI output is redacted. Runtime manifests check that no
secret value was baked in. Review clones may inject HTTPS credentials into an individual git command, but never leave them in the checkout's origin URL or any evidence artifact.
Scoped bearer tokens separate read, write, agent, dispatch, secret and admin authority. Egress policy is declared per project and per task rather than assumed.
Tenants, users, Personas and platform bindings are modelled as records, which is what lets one hub serve more than one owner without sharing credentials.
